chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Army and Navy base shows as Armstrong's music director
summary: Airlifted to bases for two concerts a day, the band played a secret B-29 plant in Arizona without leaving the vehicle.

blocks.x: Now tell us about the straw boss. What does the straw boss do?
That's what I'm telling you.
He's got all the headaches.
All the headaches. And you get it straight from the office. Get it from the office.
Like, when I was with -- I'll give you a good incident what the straw boss -- the best thing -- Like, when you're working with a guy like Louie Armstrong, who don't want no responsibility of nothing.
He's going to play his horn, he's going to do those dates. You call the rehearsal, you tell him what you want him to do.
He don't tell you nothing. You tell Louie you're going to rehearse Tuesday at 2:30 and so
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
and so -- Denver or Cleveland when we was on the road.
We got a Coca-Cola show, we got to be there to rehearse that show. And after that, we going to do so and so and so.
We were in Portland and we were travelling doing these Army and Navy shows during the world war on the bases.
Entertaining the soldiers going overseas and things like that. And we had did so many. Like the Navy Hospital, we did Washington, and we did them all over the country.
We do like the Navy or the Marines. We do like for the Army. We was doing like two concerts a day at the Army and Navy bases, and playing a dance that night.
Why we had to do that was because the Army and Navy flew us around. We couldn't get transportation.
So we were doing the Coca-Cola shows, and the Army and Navy bases. Like we'd go up to two -- we were playing in California. We flew out
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
to California, Tucson. for two {inaudible}.
They were building those B-29's that would bomb Japan at that time. We played that base,-- they sneaked us in.
Like security was so tight, we couldn't even see nothing. The truck brought us up -- the Army truck --
We get off the plane, they load us up in the Army truck, brought us right up to the auditorium.
Back the truck up, we got off and went inside, all dressed up and played the concert. Right into the trucks, right back to the plane.
You didn't even set foot on the ground.
Not on the ground. That security was so tight there.
Played for all those pilots and the captains, and everything like that.
